strengths: Rigorous theoretical foundation with formal proofs of unbiasedness, variance scaling, and concentration bounds
Well-engineered GPU kernel implementation addressing real systems challenges (sampling parallelization), with clear trade-offs between S²ANTA-prop and S²ANTA-flash documented

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple models (Llama-3.1-8B, DeepSeek-7B, BitNet-2B), benchmarks (GSM8K, MMLU, RULER), with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals and proper ablations (one-hot attention analysis revealing layer-wise importance)
Demonstrates measurable 1.5× decode-step kernel speedup on modern hardware while matching baseline accuracy
Reproducible research with open-sourced kernels, extensive pseudocode, detailed measurement protocols, and explicit cache-thrashing procedures
Honest acknowledgment of limitations (prefill doesn't benefit, requires S tuning, speedup subject to Amdahl's Law)
Thoughtful ablations including RL-based layer-wise budget optimization showing that attention importance is non-uniform across layers
weaknesses: Limited to decode stage only—paper shows prefill needs >94% unique V-row coverage (Table 9), so real-world speedup with realistic prefill/decode splits is likely much lower than 1.5×; no end-to-end inference timing measurements provided

Accuracy-efficiency trade-offs poorly characterized: S²ANTA-sys requires S=256 (~74% of sequence length) to match baseline on MMLU, suggesting practitioners need substantial S budgets; no clear guidance provided for choosing S as function of context length and target accuracy on new tasks
S²ANTA-flash suffers severe sample waste, requiring S=2048 vs. S=128 for S²ANTA-prop (16× difference), substantially limiting its appeal despite removing synchronization barrier

Bernoulli qK^T component underdeveloped: tested mainly on atypical BitNet-2B architecture, shows ~30% L2 norm error, requires additional multiplications in mean-group-query fix (Eq. 6) that undermines 'multiplier-free' claims, achieves only 15% combined access reduction (Table 7)
Hardware-specific results (RTX 6000 Ada only) with unclear generalization to other accelerators; speculative claims about future 'adder-centric' hardware
Sampling overhead not explicitly quantified or included in kernel timing analysis; sampling S indices per query could be non-trivial
Incomplete comparison to sparse attention literature—main baseline is top-k; limited comparison to other recent approximate attention methods (LSH-based, learned masks, etc.)
Key limitations relegated to appendices: prefill bottleneck and S-tuning requirements should be prominent in main paper, not buried
Paper scope unfocused: covers decode, prefill, value stage, score stage across 23 pages plus 18 appendices; Bernoulli qK^T feels disconnected from main SANTA contribution

strengths: Sound mathematical foundation with rigorous proofs of unbiasedness and variance scaling (1/S); clear advantage over biased methods like top-k
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks (GSM8K, MMLU, RULER, LongBench v2), models (Llama, DeepSeek, BitNet), and careful use of bootstrap confidence intervals
Practical GPU implementations (S²ANTA-prop and S²ANTA-flash) demonstrating measured speedups (1.5× decode-step, 1.25× end-to-end) with honest accounting of sample-waste trade-offs
Exemplary reproducibility with detailed pseudocode, measurement protocols, ablation studies, and sensitivity analyses; transparent about limitations (e.g., no benefit for prefill)
Addresses real problem in memory-bound long-context LLM inference with forward-looking energy efficiency perspective (5× reduction vs. top-k)
weaknesses: Algorithmic novelty is incremental; stochastic sampling and variance reduction via stratified/systematic sampling are standard statistical techniques; contribution is primarily in engineering execution

Speedups are modest (1.25-1.5×) and highly workload-dependent on bandwidth constraints, context length, and batch size; specialized to decode-heavy long-context regime with limited benefit for prefill or short-context inference

Bernoulli qK^T sampling component is underdeveloped and less convincing; achieves only 63.8% accuracy on GSM8K when combined with SANTA (2% drop), shows model-dependent behavior (e.g., 67.5% key access on BitNet vs. 72.8% on Llama), and lacks broad validation

Claims of complementarity with quantization/compression methods not empirically validated; applicability constrained to specific bandwidth-bound workloads and requires custom CUDA kernels limiting adoption
Systematic sampling (S²ANTA-sys) used in main results but lacks variance-reduction guarantee despite Section 3.4 relying on it; theoretical justification only for stratified variant
